clips.why: Agent memory maintenance: 'retire' is different from delete -- invalidate old facts with a time range; worked example (1,000 GitHub stars in 25 days, then 1.3k) shows why the old fact is kept for tracing. Starting at 457.5 adds the full add/delete/overwrite/no-op list as setup; both work.

Plain explanation of RAG: 'food' is embedded as a vector and similar vectors (apple, sausages) are retrieved -- semantic search instead of keywords. Starts at 'retrieval augmented generation' to drop the 'third one is' list marker.

'Reflect' merges or drops duplicate and outdated memories, linked to what Anthropic calls dreaming: while the agent is idle, schedule it to reflect and consolidate -- a post-process step. Opening at 551.7 on the dreaming line also works since the idea is re-explained; the 'last but not least' run-up is dropped.

also_ok.why: Intro fact: an LLM call carries nothing long-term; ChatGPT and Claude Code remember you because of a memory system built into their harness. Self-contained but only ~18s.

'Do nothing' retrieval: a short memory.md is just always loaded, which is part of why Claude Code's context usage looks huge (along with tool and MCP definitions). Has a light back-reference to an earlier screen.

negatives.why: Repo plug: open-source Waku agent, 1.3k stars, thanks and pip install -- self-promotion.
Arena results read off the dashboard: 4.6 s for SQLite, 7.5 s for LangMem, 'the answer is correct' -- numbers that only mean anything with the screen.
'Maybe graph memory is overkill for smaller use cases' -- sounds like a take, but its support is the Zep graph on screen and the wait before it.
'Zep team, if you're watching, please fix speed' -- a callout whose support is the preceding minutes of waiting on the demo.
